extracted.intended_audience: Noncitizen Liberians covered by DED (and persons having no nationality who last habitually resided in Liberia), their employers, and federal/state/local agencies and practitioners assisting them
extracted.subtask_description: USCIS Federal Register notice explaining who is eligible for Deferred Enforced Departure (DED)–based employment authorization for Liberians, what forms/documents to file, filing addresses and procedures, employer/agency verification rules, travel authorization, and related processes and protections. Targets issuance and use of DED-based Employment Authorization Documents (EADs) valid through June 30, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for DED-based employment authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to noncitizens of the United States who are nationals of Liberia (or persons having no nationality who last habitually resided in Liberia) who have been continuously physically present in the United States since May 20, 2017, and who were eligible for a grant of DED under the President's 2022 memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liberians must meet all eligibility criteria, including required documentation, described in this notice and in the President's memorandum. Eligibility is determined consistent with the terms of the Presidential memorandum and relevant DHS implementing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility/Exclusions from DED coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories of individuals are excluded from DED-based employment authorization even if they otherwise meet presence/nationality criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include: (1) individuals who would be ineligible for TPS for reasons in INA section 244(c)(2)(B) (8 U.S.C. 1254a(c)(2)(B)); (2) individuals who sought LRIF LPR status but whose applications were or are denied under NDAA sections 7611(b)(1)(C) and (b)(3); (3) individuals whose removal the Secretary determines is in the interest of the United States (subject to LRIF); (4) individuals whose presence or activities the Secretary of State reasonably believes would have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences; (5) individuals who voluntarily returned to Liberia or their last habitual residence for an aggregate of 180 days or more as specified in the LRIF provision; and (6) individuals subject to extradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file Form I-765 to obtain a DED-based EAD
rubrics_metrics.description: If covered by DED and wishing to obtain an EAD, you must file Form I-765.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully follow Form I-765 instructions. Indicate DED eligibility by entering “(a)(11)” in response to Question 27 on Form I-765. Submit the required fee or request a fee waiver on Form I-912. USCIS will issue a Request for Evidence (RFE) if additional information is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documentation for Form I-765
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit the supporting documents listed in the Form I-765 filing instructions to demonstrate eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Form I-765 instructions list all documents needed; additional information on initial required documents is on the USCIS I-765 webpage. If USCIS determines more evidence is needed after review, USCIS will send a request for evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment and fee waiver procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit the fee for Form I-765 unless they request and qualify for a fee waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the current fee on the Form I-765 page. Fee waiver requests may be filed on Form I-912 (see USCIS fee-waiver guidance). When filing multiple applications, USCIS recommends separate payments for each application because a single payment covering multiple applications could result in rejecting all if one is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometrics requirement and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will require biometrics for producing an EAD if necessary and will send a biometric services appointment notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you must submit biometrics, USCIS will notify you of the appointment time and location. Prepare by visiting the USCIS guidance on preparing for a biometric services appointment and bring valid photo identification. No biometrics fee is required when you file a DED-based Form I-765.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit completed DED-based Form I-765 (mailing addresses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail your completed Form I-765 and supporting documentation to the addresses specified for DED Liberia filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 provides addresses: Using USPS: USCIS, Attn: DED Liberia, P.O. Box 805283, Chicago, IL 60680-5283. Using FedEx/UPS/DHL: USCIS, Attn: DED Liberia, (Box 805283), 131 S Dearborn Street, 3rd Floor, Chicago, IL 60603-5517. Form I-765 and Form I-131 may be filed together or separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing not available
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not file a DED-based Form I-765 electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All DED-based Form I-765 submissions must be mailed to the addresses in Table 1; electronic filing is explicitly unavailable for these DED-based filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic extension of certain existing DED-based EADs through June 30, 2026
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice automatically extends DED-based EADs bearing Category Code (a)(11) and a Card Expires date of March 30, 2020; January 10, 2021; June 30, 2022; or June 30, 2024 through June 30, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EAD is valid through June 30, 2026 even if the date on the face of the card has passed. This automatic extension applies regardless of country of birth for individuals covered by DED under the June 28, 2024 memorandum. After June 30, 2026, employers can no longer accept these (a)(11) EADs with a Card Expires date of June 30, 2026; employees will need to present other evidence of employment authorization by July 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel authorization requirement and consequences of unauthorized travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberians covered by DED may apply for travel authorization by filing Form I-131; travel authorization is discretionary and required to travel and reenter the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may file Form I-131 together with Form I-765 or separately. If you leave the United States without first receiving travel authorization, you may no longer be eligible for DED and may not be permitted to reenter the United States. Returning to Liberia or your last habitual residence may affect eligibility (voluntary return 180+ days exclusion). Carefully review Form I-131 instructions when filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No biometrics fees required when filing
rubrics_metrics.description: No separate biometrics fee is required when you file a DED-based Form I-765.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will notify you if biometrics are required and will schedule an appointment; applicants should bring valid photo ID to the biometrics appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-765 and Form I-131 filing together or separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may file Form I-765 (EAD) and Form I-131 (travel document) together or separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS recommends separate payments if filing multiple applications to avoid rejection of all applications if one is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-9 documentation and timing rules for employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must present acceptable documents for Form I-9 within three business days of hire to verify identity and employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees may present any List A document (evidence of both identity and employment authorization) or a combination of List B (identity) plus List C (employment authorization), or an acceptable receipt as described in the Form I-9 instructions. An EAD is an acceptable List A document. Employers may not reject a document based on a future expiration date and must accept unexpired documents that reasonably appear to be genuine and relate to the employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employers may not require proof of Liberian citizenship or additional documents beyond Form I-9
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must accept documents listed on Form I-9 and may not require extra proof of Liberian citizenship or status beyond those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers are prohibited from requesting additional documentation beyond Form I-9 requirements when completing Form I-9 for new hires or reverifying current employees. If an employer rejects lawful documentation, requires additional documentation, or otherwise discriminates based on citizenship, immigration status, or national origin, employees have rights explained in the 'Note to Employees' section and can contact IER.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Verify mismatch (Tentative Nonconfirmation) and Final Nonconfirmation (FNC) procedures and worker protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers participating in E-Verify who receive a Tentative Nonconfirmation (mismatch) must inform the employee and give an opportunity to resolve it; employers may not take adverse action while the case is pending. A Final Nonconfirmation (FNC) permits termination if employment authorization cannot be confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers may not terminate, suspend, delay training, withhold or lower pay, or take adverse action during the time the case is pending. If an FNC occurs and the employer terminates, the employee may contact USCIS or IER for assistance. For information or to report discrimination in E-Verify, contact the DOJ IER Employer or Worker Hotlines; IER provides language interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAVE verification and appeal process for benefit-granting agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal, state, and local agencies may use SAVE to confirm DED coverage and employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAVE can verify coverage based on an EAD with category (a)(11) or a Form I-797 reflecting approval of Form I-765 for an (a)(11) EAD. SAVE usually provides automated responses, but delays can occur. Applicants can use CaseCheck to track SAVE verification using DOB and one immigration ID or Verification Case Number. If an agency denies benefits based solely or in part on a SAVE response, the agency must allow an appeal per its procedures. The SAVE website provides information on correcting or updating immigration records and how to request corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS case status and contact procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can check the status of their EAD or travel document requests and contact USCIS through multiple channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Case Status Online on the USCIS website, use the USCIS Contact Center, submit an online e-request, or visit local USCIS offices after the notice is published. Provided phone numbers and TTY options are available; USCIS also offers language support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of DED authorization dates and termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The DED extension at issue began June 28, 2024 and ends June 30, 2026; EADs issued under this authority are valid through June 30, 2026 (per the automatic extension for certain cards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After June 30, 2026, employers may no longer accept (a)(11) EADs with a Card Expires date of June 30, 2026; employees must present other evidence of employment authorization by July 1, 2026, if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Evidence (RFE) follow-up procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS needs additional information to adjudicate Form I-765 or Form I-131, USCIS will issue an RFE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to RFEs with requested documentation per USCIS instructions. The filing instructions and USCIS webpages list acceptable documentation; failure to respond may delay or result in denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for government agencies accepting DED evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying for federal, state, or local government benefits, applicants may need to present documents that show DED coverage or authorization to work based on DED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with the specific agency about which documents it will accept. Agencies using SAVE may verify DED coverage; if verification is incorrect, applicants can follow SAVE procedures to correct records and appeal agency decisions as needed.
